name: cards-grid

capacity.note: the grid loses scannability past four cards

density.note: a card body is one short clause, not a paragraph

description: 2–4 parallel items, similar weight, scannable in a grid.
purpose: Use when the audience needs to compare or scan a small set of options at a glance. Avoid for more than 4 items — split into multiple slides. For ordered/numbered steps, use list-steps instead.

cards.description: Each list item becomes one card. Authoring contract: a top-level bullet is the card title (renders bold by default); an indented bullet underneath carries the body text (renders normal weight via the nested-list rule).

insight.description: Optional key-insight panel above the cards.

sample:
<!-- _class: cards-grid -->

## A cards grid gives equal weight to peers.

- Parallel titles.
  - Noun phrases of similar weight, never mixed.
- Short bodies.
  - One clause each; a long card collapses the grid.
- Rank order.
  - Left to right reads strongest first.
- Four cards.
  - The hard ceiling; five means a new slide.

stressDoc.summary: Four cards at the hard budget.
stressDoc.sample:
<!-- _class: cards-grid -->

## Four full cards is this grid's loud maximum.

- Card one.
  - A body at the hard budget runs this long — two clauses that read as one breath, and not a word more.
- Card two.
  - Parallel structure matters most at the ceiling; matching shapes are what keep four dense cards readable as a set.
- Card three.
  - The grid trades white space for words here; past this density the audience reads one card and skips the rest.
- Card four.
  - The hard stop. A fifth card or a longer body does not fit — split the slide or reach for list-tabular.

whenToUse.title: Parallel items
whenToUse.body: Four cards or fewer, each item gets equal weight in the layout. Audience compares them at a glance.

whenToUse.title: Scannable at a glance
whenToUse.body: The audience absorbs the whole set in one look — no scrolling, no eye-leaping between rows.

whenToUse.title: Equal information density
whenToUse.body: Each card carries roughly the same text length. Uneven density makes the grid feel unbalanced.

whenToUse.title: Order is decorative
whenToUse.body: When sequence carries meaning, use list-steps or list-criteria instead. cards-grid is for parallel options.

antiPatterns.title: More than 4 items
antiPatterns.body: Split into multiple slides instead. The grid loses scannability past 4 cards.

antiPatterns.title: Order carries meaning
antiPatterns.body: Use list-steps or list-criteria. cards-grid is for parallel options, not sequences.

antiPatterns.title: Lopsided density
antiPatterns.body: Equalize the prose when one card has three sentences and the rest have one. Otherwise change layout.

antiPatterns.title: Inline-code-only body
antiPatterns.body: A body bullet containing only `code` gets promoted to an eyebrow label. Mix it with surrounding prose.

related.name: cards-stack
related.when: items stack vertically as full-width rows

three.label: Three columns
three.sample:
<!-- _class: cards-grid three -->

## three widens the grid to three columns.

- Wider cards.
  - Each card earns a third of the row.
- Same budget.
  - Bodies stay one clause, titles stay parallel.
- Sweet spot.
  - Three peers is the count this grid loves.

four.label: Four columns
four.sample:
<!-- _class: cards-grid four compact -->

## four locks a two-by-two, compact tightens it.

- Quadrant read.
  - Four cells scan as a loop.
- Compact pairing.
  - Padding shrinks so labels stay whole.
- Named corners.
  - Position carries meaning; place cards deliberately.
- Still four.
  - The ceiling does not move.

numbered.label: Numbered cards
numbered.sample:
<!-- _class: cards-grid -->

## An ordered list numbers the cards.

1. Numbers appear
   - Markdown's ordered list turns cards into steps.
2. Sequence reads
   - The grid now implies order, so mean it.
3. Budget holds
   - Same one-clause bodies as the unnumbered grid.

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing the card as one inline line (`- **Title.** body`) instead of a nested bullet.
commonMistakes.fix: cards-grid requires the nested `- Title` / `  - body` format (HARD RULE #5, lint-enforced) — the inline form fails the deck-authoring lint, and the body inherits the parent li's bold weight instead of rendering at normal weight.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a `numbered` class to the slide, expecting it to turn on corner numbers.
commonMistakes.fix: There is no `numbered` CSS class — the numbering comes purely from authoring the cards as an ordered list (`1.`) instead of a bullet list (`-`); the `numbered` entry in variants documents that authoring choice, not a class to type.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: Two cards, or the default column count already fits — no need to force a specific column count.
Exactly three parallel items need equal width — widens the grid to three columns.
Four parallel items, often a 2×2 quadrant read where card position itself carries meaning.
The cards have an implicit rank or step order worth surfacing as corner numbers — author with `1.` instead of `-`.
